name: Fan
author: E. T. Carter
description: Pleated cloth fanned around a pivot just below the frame: the folds radiate outward, narrow and converging near the pivot and opening into broad wedges toward the top, like a folding hand-fan or a sunburst-pleated skirt. Each wedge is flat-shaded into a lit plane and a shadow plane split by a luminous radial crease, and a broad band of light sweeps angularly across the fan, handing brightness wedge to wedge while the pleats ripple and breathe. A radial sibling of Pleat's straight vertical accordion.

params.label: Pleat count
params.effect: Number of pleats across a 90-degree span; few makes bold architectural wedges, many makes a fine sunburst rib.

params.label: Roll speed
params.effect: How fast the illumination band sweeps angularly across the fan; at 0 the light rests while only the cloth ripples.

params.label: Flutter
params.effect: Amplitude of the radial ripple and lean, from a rigid pressed fan to softly fluttering cloth.
